land.text: the Electorate of Saxony, raised to a kingdom on 20 December 1806
the state as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918 (Free State of Saxony)

successors.note: The state was a federal state of the German Empire from 1871 and ended in November 1918 (see the dissolve event); the Weimar Republic took over its land (Free State of Saxony). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-53 D01, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire; same change as fx-46 R122 for Bavaria); the hierarchy.csv row kingdom-of-saxony -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.

keyframe_review.note: 33,990 km2 for the new kingdom (20 December 1806). The Saxony page gives no area in km2 or square miles, so only its '60% of its land' lost in 1815 can be tested: 34,053 km2 x 0.4 = 13,600 km2 against Cliopatria's 18,212 km2 for 1820 (ratio 1.34, within the factor of two). Shape unverified in detail: page gives no pre-1815 boundary.

34,053 km2. Four cells are added around 14.06-14.44E, 51.98-52.22N (north of Cottbus; Cottbus itself is already inside the 1806 cells), the only 1807 change, and the page records 'In 1807 the Treaties of Tilsit ceded the Lordship of Cottbus' without giving a boundary. The Duchy of Warsaw page: the Duchy 'was held in personal union' by Frederick Augustus I from July 1807, but is not Saxon territory, so it is not in this shape.

correction.text: the full kingdom of 1807 including Cottbus; no cession recorded for 1809-1810

keyframe_review.note: The 1809-1810 shape (31,199 km2) loses 13 cells (about 3,300 km2) east of Dresden around Bautzen and Hoyerswerda (13.85-14.37E, 50.87-51.61N) and regains them in 1811. No opened page records a Saxon cession or occupation in 1809-1810 (the Saxony page is silent on 1809; the Duchy of Warsaw page records only Austria's cession of West Galicia to the Duchy on 14 October 1809). A hole in Saxony would be nobody's land, so the 1807 shape is kept.

34,053 km2, identical in cells to the 1807 shape; the kingdom within the Confederation of the Rhine, which it joined on 11 December 1806 and, per the Saxony page, kept 'until its dissolution in 1813'.

correction.text: the whole kingdom of 1811 under Prussian occupation and administration, 1813 to mid-1815

keyframe_review.note: 24,400 km2 with Leipzig, Torgau, Wittenberg, Merseburg and the Thuringian Circle cut off but Lower and Upper Lusatia and Cottbus still in, a partition no opened page describes. The Saxony page: the allies 'put Saxony under Prussian occupation and administration' (infobox 'Occupied by Prussia: 1813') and only at the Final Act of 9 June 1815 did the kingdom lose 'about 60% of its land'; Leipzig stays Saxon in 1815 (it is in the 1820 shape). For 1814 the state is the whole 1811 kingdom under occupation (ledger occupation events).

correction.text: Saxony after the Final Act of 9 June 1815, with the 1820 boundary

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1815-1819, which Cliopatria lacks (its shapes jump from 1814 to 1820). After the Final Act of the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815) Saxony kept the 1820 shape: 'Prussia received 60 percent of Saxony' (Vienna page); 'the kingdom had lost about 60% of its land and 40% of its population' to Prussia: Wittenberg, Lower Lusatia, most of Upper Lusatia, the Thuringian Circle and parts of the Neustadt Circle (Saxony page).

18,212 km2 for 1820-1865: 53% of the 1811 shape, against 'about 60% of its land' lost (ratio of remaining land 1.34 times the 40% the page implies, within the factor of two). Wittenberg, Lower Lusatia and the Thuringian Circle are out, Leipzig, Dresden, Bautzen, Torgau and the Vogtland are in. No area in km2 on the page; unchanged cells for 45 years, consistent with no territorial event on the Saxony page.

correction.text: the unchanged kingdom of 1820-1865, occupied by Prussia from 15 June 1866 but not annexed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1866-1867, which Cliopatria lacks (the shapes run to 1865 and resume in 1868). The Austro-Prussian War page: 'The Prussian Army invaded Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse on 15 June'; Saxony was 'Spared from annexation but joined the North German Confederation in the following year'; the Saxony page adds that 'the Austrians and French insisted Saxony be spared, and the Prussians acquiesced'. The territory is the 1820 shape throughout.
18,212 km2, the unchanged kingdom as a member of the North German Confederation (Saxony page infobox: member 1866; text: 'the next year'; the Cliopatria row for the confederation begins in 1868).
18,212 km2, unchanged; in 1871 the kingdom becomes a state of the German Empire (infobox 1 January 1871; the text dates the founding 18 January 1871).

region.text: the Electorate of Saxony raised to a kingdom

ledger.note: 1806: Saxony becomes a kingdom. 'On 20 December 1806 Frederick Augustus III, the last elector of Saxony, became King Frederick Augustus I'; the electorate had joined the Confederation of the Rhine on 11 December 1806 (infobox, Treaty of Poznań). The page names no boundary.
1807: Cottbus passes to Saxony. 'In 1807 the Treaties of Tilsit ceded the Lordship of Cottbus' (the Duchy of Warsaw page dates the Treaties of Tilsit 7 and 9 July 1807).

region.text: the whole kingdom, put 'under Prussian occupation and administration' after Leipzig

ledger.note: 1813: Prussia occupies Saxony. Infobox 'Occupied by Prussia: 1813'; 'Saxony remained within the Confederation until its dissolution in 1813 with Napoleon's defeat at the Battle of Leipzig' (the Confederation page: Leipzig 19 October, dissolution 4 November 1813). No month on the Saxony page.

region.text: Wittenberg, Lower Lusatia, most of Upper Lusatia, the Thuringian Circle and parts of the Neustadt Circle

ledger.note: 1815: Saxony loses about 60% of its land. 'the kingdom had lost about 60% of its land and 40% of its population'; infobox 'Final Act of the Congress of Vienna: 9 June 1815'; most of the Neustadt Circle parts were re-ceded by Prussia to Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach. The Vienna page: 'Prussia received 60 percent of Saxony'. The region is the 1811 shape minus the 1820 shape.

1815: page silent on the day the Prussian administration ended. The Final Act of 9 June 1815 'embodying all the separate treaties' settles Saxony's borders; the end of the occupation is placed there by the researcher. The Saxony page says only 'Occupied by Prussia: 1813'.
1866: Prussia invades Saxony. 'The Prussian Army invaded Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse on 15 June.' Saxony 'sided with Austria' (Saxony page).

1866: page silent on the date the Prussian troops left. The Peace of Prague of 23 August 1866 ended the war; Saxony was 'Spared from annexation' and joined the North German Confederation (Saxony page: 1866; text: 'the next year'). Month is the war's end, not a documented withdrawal.

region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: 13 November 1918: the king abdicates. Infobox 'Frederick Augustus III abdicates: 13 November 1918'; the kingdom was reorganized into the Free State of Saxony ('Free State established: 1 November 1920' in the infobox); infobox status 'Federal state of the German Empire (1871-1918)'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition (Saxony 1813)

zones.text: Saxony, where the allies defeated Napoleon at Leipzig and then occupied the kingdom

wars.outcome: Saxony, Napoleon's ally, is occupied by Prussia from 1813 and loses about 60% of its land to Prussia at the Congress of Vienna (Final Act, 9 June 1815).
wars.note: Named after the Confederation page's 19 October 1813 (Leipzig) and 4 November 1813 (dissolution); no Saxon battles other than Leipzig are on the opened pages, so no contest events are recorded.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussia invades Saxony on 15 June 1866 but, with Austrian and French insistence, spares it from annexation; Saxony joins the North German Confederation.

certainty.note: Napoleonic boundaries with exclaves; no opened page gives the Saxon frontier; the 1813-1815 occupation is not a border.

The 1815 Congress of Vienna boundary with Prussia, unchanged to 1871; the Thuringian exclaves and the Lusatian line are below the 253 km2 grid cell. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes:
END YEAR: 1871/1 (state of the German Empire); the monarchy lasted to 1918.
GAPS IN CLIOPATRIA: no shape for 1815-1819 and 1866-1867; both are new keyframes taken from the neighbouring Cliopatria shape. The 1814 shape is rejected as an unexplained partition.
1809-1810: Cliopatria's dip east of Dresden is not supported by any opened page; the 1807 shape is used (Saxony page silent on 1809; page budget 5: Saxony, Congress of Vienna, Confederation of the Rhine, Duchy of Warsaw, Austro-Prussian War).
DUCHY OF WARSAW: held in personal union by Frederick Augustus I from July 1807; the page says it was not Saxon territory, so there are no vassal events here (the Duchy of Warsaw dossier carries the Saxon king as duke). 1815 end of the Duchy: Final Act, 9 June 1815.
CONFLICTS: Saxony joined the North German Confederation in 1866 (infobox) or 'the next year' (text); the 1920 vs 1918 end of the monarchy; the Confederation page dates the 12 July 1806 founding where the mediatisation page says 12 June.
RULERS omitted: the Saxony page lists only Frederick Augustus I (1806-1827) and Frederick Augustus III (1904-1918).
UNVERIFIED: the exact Prussian-occupation end in 1815 and 1866 (confidence 1); the 1806 shape in detail; the Neustadt Circle land re-ceded to Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach (no separate Saxon event).
GAZETTEER: Lower Lusatia and Upper Lusatia are not regions in the gazetteer (the 1811 minus 1820 shape stands in for them). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (kingdom-of-saxony_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row kingdom-of-saxony -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. The Free State of Saxony was established on 1 November 1920 (infobox); it has no dossier of its own.
